prompt: A CI job obtains a valid OIDC token but cloud role assumption is denied. Diagnose without granting broad access.
directAnswer: Bind issuer, tenant, immutable job subject, audience, signature key, issuance/time, repository/workflow/ref claims, target role, trust mapping, conditions, session duration, requested action/resource and explicit or inherited deny. Decoding the JWT is not verification, and successful issuance is not target authorization. Preserve the denial reason, compare the exact tuple with the approved workload contract, correct the narrow mapping or permission, rerun positive and wrong-repository/audience/fork negative tests, and correlate source subject through target audit without logging the token.
foundation: Federated authentication, token exchange and resource authorization are separate decisions.
reasoningSteps: Bind safe subject and issuer metadata.
Run positive and meaningful negative tests.
Verify audit attribution without token exposure.
seniorAnswer: I preserve the denial as useful evidence and refuse administrator access. I prove both the intended allow and unintended denies while protecting the bearer credential.
weakAnswer: The token looks valid, so attach administrator to the CI role.
whyWeak: Validity does not establish intended audience, trusted tenant, assumption conditions or least-privilege resource authorization.

followUps.answer: Mutable or reusable names can transfer old permissions to another identity.
It prevents an assertion intended for one relying party from being replayed at another.
A bearer token can authorize anyone who obtains it until expiry or revocation.
